executive_summary: GBP/USD trades at 1.35243 (gated price store, close of 2026-09-03), meaning one pound buys 1.35243 US dollars; a rising pair is sterling strengthening, a falling pair is the dollar strengthening. On the payload's own figures the pair is up 0.41% over one month, 1.39% over three and 0.79% over six, and down 0.89% over twelve — it sits at the 65th percentile of its 52-week closing range, has printed higher lows at every monthly interval since late June, and made a marginal higher high on 21 August at 1.36752 intraday. The dominant bilateral narrative points the other way, and it is dated rather than atmospheric: the Federal Reserve is the only G10 central bank the market expects to raise rates, decides on 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections attached against 57-66% priced, and the Bank of England follows 24 hours later with roughly +7bp priced — a sequence that flips the bilateral policy differential from +12.5bp in sterling's favour to −12.5bp inside a single day, in a pair whose realised roll premium of 7.7bp annualised gives holders no carry cushion whatsoever. Three differentials diverge sharply from the standalone dossier views: the two current account deficits are almost identical at −2.84% and −2.85% of GDP, so the external story is composition and financing privilege rather than a gap in levels; the fiscal transmission is asymmetric, with rising long yields currently buying dollars and selling sterling even though the US sovereign arithmetic is the weaker of the two; and near-balanced goods trade of roughly $146bn two-way removes bilateral trade friction as a driver entirely. Positioning is a genuine wash — specs are short sterling and long dollars, but both legs have been reduced for weeks — while the pair's own option skew is negative at every tenor and deepens with maturity, from −0.343% at 38.6 days to −0.728% at 185.7 days, so the downside is already the paid-for side of the surface. The settled verdict is Bearish on both horizons, conviction 3 tactically (score −0.3929, confidence 61) and conviction 3 strategically (score −0.4316, confidence 58) — and the honest caveat, stated in this report's own voice, is that the price structure delivered after the scoring pass does not corroborate it: a shallow but intact sequence of higher lows, positive one-, three- and six-month returns, and an August break above the 1.35474-1.36044 supply band are the market's current answer to the same fundamentals, and the trade therefore depends on the 16-17 September cluster converting fundamentals into price rather than on momentum already doing so.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no free PPP source for this pair, so valuation is expressed as a BIS real effective exchange rate relative, and it is labelled as a proxy rather than a fair value. Sterling's REER of 111.41 (June 2026) stands 3.31% above the dollar's 107.84, which would equalise at a GBP/USD of roughly 1.3103 — spot at 1.35243 is 3.2% above that proxy, and the dollar dossier reaches the mirror figure of 1.3115 independently. Both legs are therefore expensive in real terms against the rest of the G10, and sterling marginally the more so; the pair is modestly rich rather than dislocated. What the current level prices is a pair that has already been paid its rate advantage: at the 65th closing percentile with a +12.5bp policy differential and a 7.7bp realised roll, the market is valuing sterling on a carry premium that is about to invert rather than on any growth or external improvement.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Cable is the one G10 major that cannot be held for yield in either direction, and that single fact conditions the whole trade. The bilateral policy differential is +12.5bp in sterling's favour — Bank Rate 3.75% as of 2026-08-28 against a fed funds midpoint of 3.625% as of 2026-09-01 — worth about 17 pips a year on payload spot. The realised roll premium from the gated store is +7.7bp annualised, which by covered interest parity implies a GBP/USD basis of roughly −5bp, carried with a tenor mismatch flag; this contradicts the sterling dossier's 0.0bp roll premium observed 26 August, and the gated store governs since at these magnitudes the discrepancy changes nothing. Carry-to-volatility ratio is 0.02 on policy carry and 0.012 on the realised roll — both indistinguishable from zero. Carry regime is absent and structurally so: unlike GBP/CHF at 375bp, USD/JPY at 262.5bp or GBP/SEK at 200bp, neither leg of cable is paid to be patient, so there is no yield-driven stabiliser to absorb a repricing and no cost to expressing a directional view. A flat forward curve in a pair the market has spent the year calling a carry destination is quietly consistent with the bearish case rather than the bullish one: nobody is paying to hold sterling forward.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is +12.5bp in sterling's favour, Bank Rate 3.75 percent as of 2026-08-28 against a fed funds midpoint of 3.625 percent as of 2026-09-01, and the ten-year differential is +32.6bp with both legs drawn from the same 2026-06-01 monthly vintage and therefore not quotable as a live spread. The level is nearly irrelevant to this pair: the gated calendar-spread premium is +7.7bp annualised over 13.6 to 48.6 days, which against a 3-month ATM implied volatility of 6.24 percent gives a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.02, so cable is a pure directional trade with essentially no carry to defend it. What matters is trajectory, and it is dated. The FOMC decides on 2026-09-16 with a Summary of Economic Projections attached, against 57-66 percent priced in fed funds futures for a 25bp hike and a June median dot of 3.8 percent for 2026 that implies one outright; the MPC follows on 2026-09-17 with roughly +7bp priced and 56 of 64 economists in a mid-August Reuters poll expecting no change through year-end. Delivery flips the differential to −12.5bp inside 24 hours. Transmission is direct and unusually clean: with no carry offset and a two-day decision sequence in which the Fed moves first and sets the tone, the front-end differential is close to being the whole pair over four weeks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential stops widening and becomes a persistence question, which is why confidence falls eleven points. The Federal Reserve's own June projections carry a 2026 median of 3.8 percent and a 2027 median of 3.6 percent, so on the Committee's arithmetic the September move is terminal and the next one is a cut; that makes the dollar leg a fading rather than a growing support. Against that, the Bank of England's six-month distribution is roughly 3.50 to 4.00 percent with three standing hawks who vote again at the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report, a full projection round, while the incoming labour evidence leans dovish with private-sector regular pay at 2.8 percent and payrolled employees down 210,000 on the year. The 2026-12-09 FOMC carries the next SEP and is where the 2027 cut is either confirmed or removed; the 2026-12-17 MPC is where the 2027 pay-settlement evidence the July minutes named as decisive should be visible. Net, the bilateral differential is more likely to sit at or slightly below zero for sterling through the window than to recover to its current +12.5bp, and with a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.02 there is nothing in the roll to compensate a holder of the pair for waiting.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential runs in the dollar's favour on the measure that actually drives policy. US core PCE has been stuck at 3.3 percent for three consecutive months with headline PCE at 3.7 percent and a six-month annualised rate of 4.1 percent, against UK core CPI at 2.6 percent and services CPI FALLING to 3.4 percent from 3.6 percent — the gauge the MPC majority relies on. So the higher-inflation economy is also the one whose central bank has tied its reaction function explicitly to that number, while the lower-inflation economy is the one whose committee has said it will look through an energy-driven headline. The growth differential points the same way: US GDP 2.1 percent year on year with an August composite PMI of 56.0 and a Q3 GDPNow of 4.8 percent, against UK GDP 1.2 percent and a composite PMI of 52.5. The surprise differential is where the tactical risk sits and it is not symmetric: US payrolls fell 23,000 in July with average hourly earnings at a five-year low of 3.2 percent, so the 2026-09-04 report is a genuine two-sided event for the pair, and 2026-09-11 US CPI lands five days before the FOMC. UK releases on 15 and 16 September matter less because the MPC outcome is already discounted. Transmission is therefore asymmetric by design this month: the pair moves more on US data than on UK data.

The unpriced item is the conditional path from a second negative US payroll print on 4 September to a Fed hold twelve days later, which is the fat left tail in this factor.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential narrows and the stance weakens accordingly. Much of the US inflation excess is a tariff level effect — an average statutory rate of 11.0 percent as at 2026-08-24 — which raises the price index once and then drops out of the year-on-year comparison, and the same is structurally true of the UK's energy-driven headline. Both labour markets are loosening: US average hourly earnings at 3.2 percent with participation down to 61.4 percent, UK private-sector regular pay at 2.8 percent against a target-consistent estimate near 3.25 percent and vacancies at their lowest since early 2021. The residual bilateral tilt is that the US retains a meaningful nominal growth advantage — 2.1 percent versus 1.2 percent year on year, with corporate profits up 8.2 percent on the quarter — while the UK is absorbing an energy shock through household real income, with real regular pay growth of only 0.5 percent. That is a slow, compounding drag on the pair rather than a sharp one, and it is why the weight falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and confidence to 52. The resolution dates are the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report and the 2026-12-09 FOMC SEP, at which each central bank marks its own view of these series to market.

Strategically both inflation excesses are level effects with finite lives and both labour markets are loosening, so the differential compresses to a nominal growth gap of 0.9 percentage points that transmits slowly.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: GBP/USD is a low-risk-beta pair: both legs are reserve or near-reserve currencies, sterling is only mildly risk-positive and the dollar is the risk-off beneficiary, so global risk indicators carry far less bilateral information here than for a pure risk proxy; extended over one to six months as the pair's dominant risk exposures become idiosyncratic to each leg rather than global.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the one factor that argues for the pair rising, and it does so weakly. The global risk environment is emphatically benign — VIX 14.43 on 28 August, down 6.23 points on the month from 20.66, US investment-grade spreads at 79bp and high yield at 260-263bp after tightening 27bp — and the bilateral sign convention means benign conditions favour the higher-beta leg, which is sterling. Cable's risk beta is genuinely low: sterling strengthens in risk-on but with far less beta than the Antipodeans, and the dollar is the haven the market buys when the VIX spikes, so the pair sits in the framework's low-sensitivity bucket alongside EUR/USD and USD/CAD. Two qualifications hold confidence at 52. First, the FTSE 250 has underperformed the FTSE 100 by roughly ten percentage points, and it is the domestically exposed index, so the UK-specific signal inside the equity complex is weaker than the headline benign reading. Second, at a 14.43 VIX and 79bp investment-grade spreads there is essentially no room left for further compression, so the distribution of outcomes from here is skewed toward risk-off, and every point of that skew is dollar-positive and therefore pair-negative. Over four weeks the level is supportive; the asymmetry is not.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the factor loses its directional content for this pair entirely and becomes a variance amplifier, which is why the strategic weight is only 0.03. The dominant risk exposure for cable across the window is idiosyncratic rather than global — the 28 October Budget on the sterling leg and the 3 November midterms on the dollar leg — and neither is forecastable from the VIX. The three identifiable regime shifts point in incompatible directions for the pair. A Hormuz re-escalation is simultaneously risk-off (dollar-positive) and a terms-of-trade shock to a net energy importer (sterling-negative), so both legs push the pair down and the factor would flip decisively bearish. A US-led equity correction as the Fed hikes into record valuations is dollar-positive and pair-negative. A durable Middle East de-escalation is risk-positive and pair-supportive but would also collapse the BoE's hawkish tail, muddying the transmission. With no single scenario carrying a high enough probability to establish direction and their pair impacts not aligned, Neutral is the honest label rather than a hedge.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The two legs' positioning is the textbook case where the pair signal is muted rather than amplified, and the honest output is Neutral. Specs are short sterling and long dollars, so the aggregate stock of positioning is short cable — that is a contrarian positive for the pair. But both legs are being reduced simultaneously: the sterling non-commercial net improved from −54,600 to −44,500 on the 28 August release, roughly 10,100 contracts of covering in a week and a sixth consecutive week of it, while dollar-index non-commercial length has been cut for four straight weeks from a 22,499-contract peak on 4 August to 18,682 on 25 August. Covering a short sterling base buys the pair; trimming a dollar long also buys the pair; so the FLOW is pair-supportive while the STOCK is pair-negative, and they roughly cancel over four weeks. Two further facts pull the same way. Sterling leveraged funds are already net LONG 40,670 contracts, 15.9 percent of open interest, on a stale 11 August tranche, meaning the fast money that would normally squeeze the pair higher has already bought; and the option market is paying for pair downside, with 25-delta risk reversals negative at −0.343 percent at 38.6 days. The residual sterling short is concentrated in asset managers at −119,863 contracts, which is hedge-driven and slow, so it is a poor source of a violent squeeze.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two structural flows on the two legs point in opposite directions and neither dominates, so Neutral again. On the sterling side the relevant flow is not futures at all but UK pension and insurance hedge ratios — the LDI channel that turned the 2022 gilt crisis into a sterling crisis — together with foreign ownership of roughly 25-30 percent of outstanding gilts; with the 30-year gilt at 5.73-5.76 percent and a Budget on 28 October, that channel is live and pair-negative if it activates, and leveraged funds sitting net long 40,670 contracts means positioning would amplify rather than absorb a Budget disappointment. On the dollar side the relevant flow is reserve-manager allocation, and it is pair-positive but slow and contested: the dollar's share of allocated reserves was 57.13 percent in 2026-Q1, having RISEN from 56.42 percent in 2025-Q4, against a 2001 peak near 72 percent, and the IMF has attributed the majority of past declines to valuation rather than active selling. The broad trade-weighted dollar falling 1.69 percent on the month against a G10-only basket down 0.37 percent is the signature of structural dollar reduction against emerging markets rather than against sterling. A slow, mostly-valuation drag on one leg against a dated amplification risk on the other is a genuine standoff.

At roughly the 30th percentile of its one-year range against a −80,000 stretched threshold, the sterling leg is not crowded; the dollar leg at roughly the 80th percentile is elevated but was cut for four consecutive weeks before the catalyst.
tactical.unwind_trigger: The double-barrel squeeze: a hot UK August CPI on 16 September, with NBP gas 18-21 percent above the BoE's own 136 pence July conditioning assumption and BRC shop prices at a two-year high of 1.5 percent, immediately followed by an MPC vote split hardening from 6-3 to 5-4 on 17 September — combined with an FOMC hold on 16 September that strands the dollar long. Any two of those three reprice the pair violently higher.
tactical.historical_analogue: The July-August 2026 sequence in this pair's own positioning: six consecutive weeks of sterling short covering from −54,600 to −44,500 lifted cable while open interest FELL 9.4 percent, the signature of a liquidation-driven rally that exhausts rather than extends. The squeeze fuel was consumed, not accumulated.
tactical.contrarian_case: The case against our bearish tactical stance is coherent and should be stated plainly. Sterling still carries the best real policy rate in the G10 at +0.85 percent, three MPC members have voted to hike at each of the last two meetings, prediction markets price the Fed hike at only 48-55 percent against futures at 57-66 percent, and the July US payroll print of −23,000 makes tightening into a contracting labour market genuinely hard to defend. If the FOMC holds on 16 September, an 18,682-contract dollar long is stranded into a market that repriced from 35.4 percent to 60.4 percent in four sessions, and the pair squeezes hard within days.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: The strategic stock is a hedge-driven asset-manager sterling short of 119,863 contracts that will not unwind on a headline, set against a dollar long at a three-and-a-half-year high with far more room to be reduced than added. Netted, positioning offers the pair neither a cushion nor a spring.
strategic.unwind_trigger: On the sterling side, a 28 October Budget that fails the fiscal mandate credibly, which forces leveraged funds to liquidate a 40,670-contract long on top of any fresh shorting. On the dollar side, a COFER print in which the reserve-share decline is attributable to active selling rather than valuation, or a failed long-end Treasury auction — either of which would reduce dollar length structurally and lift the pair.
strategic.historical_analogue: September-October 2022: sterling fell roughly 8 percent against the dollar in the fortnight around the mini-Budget precisely BECAUSE the market was not short going in, so the move was amplified by liquidation rather than absorbed by covering. The current leveraged-fund long of 40,670 contracts recreates that configuration ahead of 28 October.
strategic.contrarian_case: The strategic contrarian case is that the crowd is short the dollar, not long it: the sourceable sell-side consensus points to a mid-90s DXY on a premise of 2026 Fed cuts that the June dot plot, the 9-3 July vote and a 4.34 percent two-year have already falsified. If that consensus is forced to revise after a September hike, the dollar leg gets a second bid and the pair falls further than our own weighted score implies — so the contrarian risk here is that we are not bearish enough, which is unusual and worth stating.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: STRATEGIC ONLY: the two current account deficits are almost identical in size, UK −2.84% of GDP against US −2.85%, so the bilateral external differential is narrower than either standalone dossier implies and rests on composition and financing privilege rather than on a gap in levels.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral trade channel is neutral and the commodity channel is not, and separating the two is the whole content of this factor for cable. On IMF DOTS 2024 goods data the UK exported 73.7 billion dollars to the US and imported 72.7 billion, a net balance of just 1.0 billion on roughly 146 billion of two-way trade; the US reports the mirror as an 11.8 billion dollar surplus of its own. Neither number is large enough relative to either economy to generate a structural flow or a policy grievance, so the external channel in this pair runs through third-party energy prices and financing rather than through UK-US flows. On terms of trade the asymmetry is stark and it is not about crude. The UK is a net energy importer with front-month NBP gas at 161.02 pence per therm on 26 August and around 165 pence on 28 August, 18 to 21 percent above the Bank of England's own 136-pence July conditioning assumption and roughly 43 percent higher year on year, with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed and one-fifth of global LNG trade normally transiting it. The US is a net energy exporter. The partial offset is that Brent fell 12.0 percent on the month to 88.24 dollars, which is the one commodity leg supporting the pair — cheaper crude improves the UK import bill and is disinflationary for the US. Over four weeks the terms-of-trade channel transmits slowly, which is why the weight is 0.06, but the direction is not in doubt.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: This is the second-largest strategic weight and it is bearish for the pair, but at materially lower confidence than the sterling dossier alone would suggest, because both legs are deteriorating. The UK ran a 22.1 billion pound current account deficit in Q1 2026, 2.8 percent of GDP, with the goods deficit widening 4.0 billion to 59.5 billion while the offsetting services surplus FELL 1.2 billion to 51.8 billion, and the headline narrowing came entirely from an 8.0 billion pound primary income swing. The US ran 226.8 billion dollars, 2.9 percent of GDP, widening, with its own primary income balance flipping from surplus to deficit and a net international investment position of minus 21.27 trillion dollars; its advance goods balance deteriorated 18 billion in a single month. So the levels offset almost exactly and the differential is in two things only. First, direction of energy exposure: the UK must sell sterling to buy gas through a northern-hemisphere heating season that falls inside the window, while the US sells energy. Second, financing privilege: roughly 40-50 percent of global trade is invoiced in dollars and the dollar retains a 57 percent reserve share, whereas the UK finances a deficit of identical size through a gilt market 25-30 percent foreign-owned with no invoicing franchise. Both differentials point the pair lower; neither is large enough to justify high confidence.

Tactically the gas overshoot is a live, dated observation on one leg only, which supports the marginally higher number.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: GBP: net energy importer with no material commodity export franchise. Front-month NBP gas 161-165 pence per therm in the last week of August, 18-21% above the Bank of England's 136-pence July conditioning assumption and roughly 43% higher year on year; crude and refined products imported; direct exposure to the household energy price cap and to industrial input costs.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: USD: net energy exporter in both crude and LNG. Brent 88.24 dollars and WTI 83.90 on 25 August, Brent down 12.07 dollars or 12.0% on the month from 100.31; Henry Hub 2.70 dollars, unremarkable. Higher global energy prices are a mild terms-of-trade positive and a firm inflation impulse that reinforces a hawkish Fed.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: negative for GBP as importer, positive for USD as net exporter and additionally positive via a reinforced hawkish Fed — both legs push the pair DOWN. Natural gas and LNG up: strongly negative for GBP given the price cap and industrial cost channel, mildly positive for USD as an LNG exporter competing for Asian and European cargoes — both legs push the pair DOWN, harder than the crude channel. Oil down, which is what actually happened at minus 12.0% on the month: mildly positive for GBP through the import bill, mildly negative for USD through terms of trade but disinflationary for the US and therefore a modest brake on the hike odds that dominate Factor 1 — this leg pushes the pair UP and is the only commodity route that supports it. Netting the observed moves, gas at a 43% annual increase on a commodity the UK must import outweighs a 12% monthly fall in a crude price where the UK is a smaller marginal loser, so the net commodity effect is bearish for the pair. Critically the two legs are on opposite sides of the same shock, which means there is no cancellation of the kind AUD/CAD would show.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent to roughly 97 dollars: GBP negative through the import bill and household real income, USD positive through net-exporter terms of trade and a firmer inflation impulse into the 2026-10-28 and 2026-12-09 FOMC decisions. Net: pair falls, and the effect compounds because both legs move the same way.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent to roughly 79 dollars: GBP marginally positive on the import bill, USD marginally negative on terms of trade but more importantly disinflationary, which would soften exactly the hike odds carrying Factor 1. Net: pair rises. This is the cleanest commodity route to our being wrong and it is why the 6 September OPEC meeting matters more for cable than its size suggests.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: UK NBP natural gas, and by extension JKM LNG with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed — not crude. Gas is the UK-salient price, it is the one running 18-21% above the Bank of England's own conditioning assumption, and it is the one whose seasonal demand peak falls inside the strategic window.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The two committees look symmetric and are not. Both held at their last meeting with three members dissenting or voting hawkishly — the Fed 9-3 on 29 July with all three dissenters wanting a hike, the MPC 6-3 on 29 July with Greene, Mann and Pill wanting 4.00 percent — but the guidance-versus-pricing gaps run in opposite directions. The Fed's own June median dot of 3.8 percent for 2026 implies a hike outright while futures price only 57-66 percent, so the central bank is MORE hawkish than its curve; the MPC's majority has said it is on hold and the market prices roughly +7bp, so guidance and pricing are aligned to within a few basis points. Chair Warsh then closed the gap further at Jackson Hole on 28 August, recommitting to the 2 percent PCE objective as a firm fixed target and saying the summer readings do not tell him underlying trends have meaningfully improved, while Governor Bailey has pointed to the upward-sloping gilt curve as itself weighing on inflation pressures — an argument that the bond market has done the tightening for the MPC, and the mechanism by which bad UK fiscal news becomes dovish UK policy news. Sequencing compounds it: the FOMC decides on 2026-09-16 and the MPC on 2026-09-17, so the Fed sets the tone and the Bank responds into it rather than the reverse.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both reaction functions become genuinely symmetric and they cancel, which is why this factor contributes nothing to the strategic score despite carrying a 0.12 weight. On the sterling side the MPC has published the most explicitly two-sided guidance of its cycle: Ramsden says a hike may be warranted if risks crystallise and that he would consider resuming cuts if they subside, Taylor describes an economy drifting toward deficient demand, and three hawks argue Bank Rate should already be higher. The named unresolved input is 2027 pay settlements, with information expected towards the end of the year, which places the resolution precisely at the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report and the 2026-12-17 decision. On the dollar side the Fed's June projections carry 3.8 percent for 2026 and 3.6 percent for 2027, so the Committee's own guidance says September is terminal and the following move is a cut — which is a fading dollar support and therefore pair-supportive. Credibility is high on both legs and neither has walked back a communication this cycle; the tail risks are opposite in sign, with a US institutional-independence question that would cost the dollar its credibility premium against a UK mechanism in which fiscal stress produces dovish policy. Two credible communicators with symmetric functions and offsetting tails is a Neutral, not a hedge.

Strategically both reaction functions are symmetric — the Fed's own dots embed a 2027 cut and the MPC is explicitly two-way pending 2027 pay settlements — so the same institutional facts produce a wide, unbiased distribution and contribute nothing directional.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk in this pair is dominated by one leg for the next four weeks. The dollar leg carries the genuine binaries — August payrolls on 4 September after a minus 23,000 print, CPI on 11 September, and the FOMC on 2026-09-16 with a Summary of Economic Projections attached and 57-66 percent priced for a hike — while the sterling leg carries scheduled releases with published consensus and an MPC on 2026-09-17 whose rate outcome is already discounted at roughly +7bp. Event clustering amplifies rather than cancels: the two decisions fall within 24 hours of one another, so the pair's entire policy differential reprices in a single window, and the plausible combination of a Fed hike followed by a Bank of England hold pushes both legs the same way. The geopolitical overlay is asymmetric in the pair's favour on the bearish side: the unresolved Middle East conflict with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed is simultaneously a haven bid for the dollar and a terms-of-trade tax on a net energy importer, so escalation is doubly pair-negative. Bilateral political risk between the two economies is immaterial — near-balanced goods trade of 146 billion dollars two-way with a 1.0 billion net balance, and no dated UK-US dispute — with the shared, second-order exposure being the Section 301 tariff architecture that took effect on 24 July.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The strategic calendar contains one clustering that is specific to this pair and that no standalone dossier can see: on 2026-10-28 the UK Autumn Budget with its accompanying OBR economic and fiscal forecast lands on the SAME DAY as an FOMC decision. Both legs reprice together, and the plausible joint outcome — a fiscally strained Budget delivered by a Chancellor three months into the job under a Prime Minister who took office on 20 July, against a Fed that has just hiked and says nothing new — pushes the pair the same way twice. The sterling-leg asymmetry is the larger of the two: the OBR's March headroom of 9.9 billion pounds has almost certainly been consumed by a 39 basis point year-on-year rise in the 10-year gilt at roughly 2.5 billion pounds of debt service per 0.25 percentage point, and the fiscal rules cap the good outcome while a 30-year gilt at 5.73-5.76 percent amplifies the bad one. The dollar leg's own binary, the 3 November midterms, is genuinely two-sided through the fiscal, growth and Fed-pressure channels and cannot be assigned a direction. Adding an asymmetric, downside-skewed event on one leg to an ambiguous event on the other, in a window that also contains the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report and the 2026-12-09 FOMC SEP, yields a Bearish stance at moderate confidence.

Strategically the window acquires a genuinely asymmetric idiosyncratic event on the sterling leg — the 28 October Budget with its OBR forecast — that happens to fall on the same day as an FOMC decision, which is the one piece of event structure in this analysis that is visible only bilaterally.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: On the raw arithmetic the US sovereign position is arguably the weaker of the two — debt held by the public at 101 percent of GDP against UK public sector net debt at 95.1 percent, a deficit above 2 trillion dollars or roughly 6.5 percent of GDP against a UK 4.2 percent, projected federal interest costs of 1,039 billion dollars, and one notch better ratings at Aa1/AA+/AA+ against AA/AA-/Aa1-Aa3 — yet the pair implication is unambiguously bearish, because the TRANSMISSION is asymmetric. On 1 September a global bond rout lifted US yields and the dollar together: in the current regime a deteriorating US fiscal position is expressed as a dollar-supportive term premium. In the UK the correlation flips in stress — cable is normally positively correlated with the 30-year gilt yield and turns negative in a fiscal crisis — and the market has already repriced that risk in gilts, with a 10-year gilt-Bund spread of roughly 184 basis points, the widest since the 2022 mini-Budget, on the debt of a country whose central bank is less likely to hike than the ECB. So the same input, a rising long yield, buys the quote currency and sells the base currency. The tactical caveat is that there is no scheduled catalyst before 28 October to convert the standing UK premium into a currency move, which is why the weight is only 0.04 tactically.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: This is the highest-confidence stance in the analysis and the reason is that the sterling leg has a dated catalyst and closed arithmetic while the dollar leg has neither. The OBR's March 2026 forecast left 9.9 billion pounds of headroom against the fiscal mandate, a margin the OBR itself warned could be erased by a modest rise in borrowing costs; the 10-year gilt has since risen 39 basis points year on year at roughly 2.5 billion pounds of annual debt service per 0.25 percentage point, so the headroom has plausibly been consumed entirely, and Chancellor Healey must resolve that on 2026-10-28 with an OBR forecast attached. The dollar leg's fiscal deterioration is larger in magnitude, compounds automatically as low-coupon debt rolls into a 4.5-5.2 percent curve, and is made worse by a September hike — but it has no scheduled resolution date inside the window, S&P affirmed AA+ with a stable outlook on 26 June citing credible monetary policy execution, and the current regime converts it into a dollar-supportive term premium rather than a currency discount. A dated, asymmetric, rule-constrained event on the base leg against an undated compounding drag on the quote leg is a clear bearish configuration for the pair, and the fact that the objectively weaker sovereign is the one being rewarded is precisely the point.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The price-structure half of this factor — trend regime, moving averages, support and resistance zones, ATR — is deliberately absent from this pass and belongs to the second, which has the data for it. What this pass does have is the pair's own option surface from the gated store, and it carries a directional signal. Twenty-five delta risk reversals are negative at every tenor and monotonically deepening: minus 0.343 percent at 38.6 days, minus 0.557 at 94.7 and minus 0.728 at 185.7. Negative risk reversals mean the market pays more for sterling puts than for sterling calls, so smart money is hedging pair DOWNSIDE, and the fact that the skew steepens with tenor points the demand squarely at the 28 October Budget rather than at the September central-bank cluster. Twenty-five delta butterflies rise in step, 0.122 to 0.178 to 0.214, so fatter tails are being priced further out too. Against that, the ATM term structure is in plain contango — 5.654 percent, 6.240 and 6.645 — with no near-dated backwardation despite two policy decisions inside 24 hours in the front tenor, which says the market is charging for direction through skew but not for the event through level. Combined with a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.02, the structural read is a pair that must move on direction and whose option market already leans the way we do. Pass-two addendum — the price-structure half: the chart-based evidence that this factor was scored without does not corroborate the Bearish stance, since the three daily moving averages are within 6.2 pips of each other with spot 75-82 pips above all three, the pair has made higher lows since 24 June and a marginal higher high on 21 August, and it sits at the 65th percentile of its 52-week closing range.

The 185.7-day risk reversal at minus 0.728 percent is more than twice the front-tenor skew, and the 94.7-day tenor at minus 0.557 spans the 28 October Budget, the 5 November Monetary Policy Report and the 9 December FOMC. That is a market with a settled directional preference for pair downside over the strategic window, expressed through skew rather than through level: the ATM term premium from 38.6 to 185.7 days is only 0.99 volatility points for a period containing a Budget with an OBR forecast, a UK projection round, two Fed SEPs, a US midterm election and an unresolved conflict. So the surface corroborates the direction of the strategic verdict while telling us the level of implied volatility is cheap relative to the calendar it spans. The weight remains the framework minimum at 0.03 because a vol surface is corroboration, not a driver, and because the price-structure content that would normally sit here is not available to this pass by design.

expression_assessment.vol_landscape_summary: Cheap in level, informative in skew. ATM implied volatility runs 5.654% at 38.6 days, 6.240 at 94.7 and 6.645 at 185.7 — plain contango with no near-dated kink despite two policy decisions 24 hours apart in the front tenor — while 25-delta risk reversals are negative and deepening across the curve at minus 0.343, minus 0.557 and minus 0.728%. The market has a directional preference for pair downside and is not paying an event premium for the timing of it. With a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.02 there is no yield to earn or pay for waiting. Adding pass two's data: 20-day realised volatility of 3.87% against 5.654% front implied is a 1.78-point variance premium, so the front of the curve is expensive against delivered movement even while being cheap against the calendar — the resolution is that the surface is mispriced in shape, not level, and one standard deviation over 38.6 days is 249 pips.
expression_assessment.directional_expression: The bearish view is better bought than carried. Because the roll premium is only 7.7bp annualised, a spot expression neither costs nor earns anything meaningful, so the choice between spot and options turns entirely on the shape of the surface: front-tenor ATM at 5.654% with no event backwardation makes the September cluster unusually cheap to own outright, while the negative skew means downside strikes are the expensive side of an already-cheap surface. The practical consequence is that the cleanest expression of the tactical view is the ATM level rather than the skew, and any downside-strike structure is paying for a directional consensus that already exists. In pass-two terms: a spot short entered into the 1.3547-1.3604 supply band with a stop above 1.3625, or an at-the-money-forward put expiring after 17 September, both express the view; a 25-delta put does so at a skew-inflated price.
expression_assessment.event_timing_consideration: The surface prices the calendar backwards relative to where the events are. The 38.6-day tenor contains the 2026-09-16 FOMC with an SEP and the 2026-09-17 MPC and carries the LOWEST implied volatility on the curve; the 94.7-day tenor contains the 2026-10-28 Budget-plus-FOMC same-day cluster and the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report at only 0.59 points more. Expression should therefore be built around the two dated clusters rather than held continuously, and the tenor spanning 28 October is where the skew says the market expects the move.
expression_assessment.liquidity_note: GBP/USD is one of the three most liquid pairs in the world with continuous two-way pricing across the London and New York sessions and a listed CME options complex, so execution and gap risk are the least of the constraints here. The practical liquidity caveat is timing rather than depth: the 16-17 September window concentrates two policy outcomes into 24 hours and the 28 October window concentrates a Budget and an FOMC into a single session, so slippage risk is event-clustered rather than structural. Round-number interest at 1.3500, 1.3600 and 1.3700 is the standard barrier geography in cable; outside commentary notes that key psychological levels like 1.3500 often see profit-taking that can trigger pullbacks of 50-100 pips, which at 53 pips of ATR is one to two sessions.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Dollars are abundant and there is no funding premium in this pair, which is mildly supportive of the base currency and therefore leaves this factor with no tradeable direction over four weeks. The evidence is the basis. CME's three-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis index closed at minus 0.81 basis points on 28 August, essentially zero against minus 40 to minus 80 in historically stressed periods, and for cable specifically the gated calendar-spread premium of plus 7.7 basis points set against a plus 12.5 basis point policy differential implies a GBP/USD basis of roughly minus 5 basis points — benign, and labelled as a derivation with a tenor mismatch, since the calendar spread spans 13.6 to 48.6 days rather than three months. SOFR is reported near 3.65 percent, consistent with a 3.50-3.75 percent target range with no dislocation, there is no reported swap-line usage, and the Bank of England's standing dollar facility is inactive. Quantitative tightening ceased in December 2025 and the balance sheet is 6,731 billion dollars, up 0.3 percent year on year, so the Fed is no longer draining global liquidity. Holding this Neutral rather than counting benign funding as a pair positive also avoids double-counting the hawkish Fed repricing, which already sits in Factor 1 at a 0.27 weight.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the same setup acquires a direction, and it is pair-negative. Reserve balances are drifting down at 2,916 billion dollars toward the roughly 3 trillion minimum comfortable level, the overnight reverse repo facility that absorbed three years of tightening is empty at 702 million, and bill supply from a deficit above 2 trillion dollars now drains bank reserves directly rather than being intermediated by money funds parked at the Fed. That is the exact configuration of the fourth quarter of 2025, when SOFR-to-IORB spreads reached their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage spiked to a record 74.6 billion dollars on 31 December before collapsing to zero in January. Tighter dollar funding moves the dollar toward the left-hand, stress side of the smile, which is pair-negative — and the transmission is specifically bilateral here, because London's role in global banking makes UK institutions structurally large dollar borrowers, so the September quarter-end and the 31 December turn both fall inside the window with the sterling leg as the natural stress point. Confidence is held at 52 because the New York Fed's rebranded full-allotment standing repo operations cap the tail: the base case is periodic pressure rather than dislocation, and a basis at minus 0.81 basis points means there is no premium to erode from.

tactical.score_interpretation: Minus 0.3929 on a scale running from minus one to plus one is a clear bearish tilt for GBP/USD — the pair falls — and it is derived mechanically, since anything at or beyond minus 0.10 is Bearish. The structure is concentrated rather than broad: Policy and Rates alone contributes minus 0.1782 and Inflation and Growth minus 0.1008, so 71 percent of the gross negative comes from two factors that resolve on the same two dates, 4 September payrolls and the 16-17 September policy cluster. Seven factors contribute negatively, one positively (Risk Appetite at plus 0.0364) and two are Neutral by construction because their two legs genuinely offset. Breadth is doing some of the work here but not most of it; depth in one heavily weighted factor is doing the rest, and that is why conviction is 3 rather than 4. Mapping to conviction: an absolute score in the 0.25-0.45 band maps to conviction 3.
tactical.rationale: At the applied tactical weights Policy and Rates at 0.27 and Inflation and Growth at 0.18 carry 45 percent of the score and both point the same way, so this is substantially a relative-policy call with a growth-differential overlay. The mechanism is dated and narrow. The FOMC decides on 2026-09-16 with a Summary of Economic Projections attached against 57-66 percent priced in futures for a 25bp hike and a June median dot of 3.8 percent that implies one outright, and the MPC follows on 2026-09-17 with roughly plus 7 basis points priced and 56 of 64 economists expecting no change through year-end. Delivery flips the bilateral policy differential from plus 12.5 basis points in sterling's favour to minus 12.5 — the only sign change available in the G10 this month — and with the gated calendar-spread premium at just plus 7.7 basis points annualised and a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.02, there is no carry cushion to absorb it. The two standalone dossiers reinforce rather than conflict, sterling tactically Bearish on its own terms at minus 0.1456 and the dollar tactically Bullish at plus 0.3440, and cable is the pair where those two verdicts stack most cleanly rather than partially cancelling. Three bilateral modifiers matter. First, near-balanced goods trade — 73.7 billion dollars of UK exports against 72.7 billion of imports for a 1.0 billion net balance on IMF DOTS 2024 — means the external channel runs through third-party energy prices and financing, not through UK-US flows, so tariff and trade-dispute risk is symmetric and small. Second, the fiscal transmission is asymmetric: a bond rout on 1 September lifted US yields and the dollar together, while the UK correlation flips to sell sterling when long gilt yields rise, so the same input helps one leg and hurts the other. Third, the pair's own option skew already leans our way, with 25-delta risk reversals negative at every tenor, which confirms direction but means the trade is not undiscovered. What is priced is the 17 September hold at roughly plus 7 basis points and 57-66 percent of the Fed hike; what is not priced is the cross-currency consequence of the sign change, and that is the edge. The path of least resistance is lower into and through the 16-17 September cluster, with the second leg of any move waiting on 28 October. Dated catalysts anchor every claim: 4 September US payrolls, 11 September US CPI, 15-16 September UK labour and CPI, 16 September FOMC with SEP, 17 September MPC with its annual gilt-reduction vote. Conviction is 3 and not higher for three honest reasons: the risk regime is benign at a 14.43 VIX and 79 basis point investment-grade spreads, which mildly favours the base leg; positioning is a genuine wash, with a sterling short base still covering at roughly 10,100 contracts a week and dollar length trimmed for four consecutive weeks before Jackson Hole; and 4 September payrolls carry a fat left tail after July's minus 23,000, since a second contraction would make a hike twelve days later very hard to defend.
tactical.g10_relative_ranking: Among sterling shorts, GBP/USD ranks third of the sterling complex as a fundamental expression, behind GBP/NOK — where Norway's 15.59 percent of GDP current account surplus is funded by the identical energy prices taxing Britain and a short is paid 50bp of carry — and behind GBP/AUD on carry terms, but ahead of GBP/CHF, GBP/SEK and GBP/JPY, which are already stretched and cost 375, 200 and 275 basis points respectively to hold short. Among dollar longs it ranks second or third behind USD/CAD and USD/CHF on carry-adjusted grounds, but it is distinguished by carrying the only policy-differential SIGN CHANGE in the G10 on 16 September, which makes it the most event-clean dollar long in the set even though its carry is nil. The pair's defining characteristic relative to every peer is that it is a pure directional expression: at a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.02 neither leg is paid to be patient.

strategic.score_interpretation: Minus 0.4316 is a clear bearish result for the pair, derived mechanically from the threshold rule, and it sits just inside the conviction-3 band with the boundary to 4 at minus 0.45. Unlike the tactical score it is broadly based: six factors contribute negatively — Policy minus 0.132, External Balance minus 0.078, USD Liquidity minus 0.0624, Fiscal minus 0.062, Inflation and Growth minus 0.052 and Event Risk minus 0.029 — and none contributes positively. That absence of a positive contributor deserves an explicit caveat rather than being read as strength: the genuine strategic case for the pair rising is the deterioration in the US external and fiscal position, and it does not appear as a positive because the base currency has its own version of the same problem, of almost identical size, without the reserve-currency privilege. Three factors are Neutral because their two legs genuinely offset, so breadth here reflects consistent one-way differentials rather than manufactured agreement. Mapping to conviction: the 0.25-0.45 band maps to conviction 3; the score sits near the upper boundary and is held at 3 rather than lifted to 4 for the reasons in the rationale.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework moves weight out of Inflation and Growth and Risk Appetite and into External Balance, Guidance and Fiscal, and after pair-specific adjustment the two largest weights are Policy and Rates at 0.24 and External Balance at 0.15, with Fiscal raised to 0.10. Policy and Rates stays Bearish at reduced confidence of 55 because the differential stops widening: the Fed's own June projections carry 3.8 percent for 2026 and 3.6 percent for 2027, so the September move is terminal on the Committee's own arithmetic, while the Bank of England's six-month distribution is roughly 3.50-4.00 percent with three standing hawks voting again at the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report. External Balance is the second-largest weight and it is bearish for the pair, but at only 52 confidence, and the reason is a genuinely bilateral discovery: the two current account deficits are almost identical, UK minus 2.84 percent of GDP against US minus 2.85 percent, so the differential is not in the level but in two things — the direction of energy exposure, since the UK must sell sterling to buy gas at 161-165 pence per therm against the Bank of England's own 136-pence conditioning assumption through a heating season that falls inside the window, while the US is a net energy exporter; and financing privilege, since roughly 40-50 percent of global trade is invoiced in dollars against a UK deficit of identical size financed through a gilt market 25-30 percent foreign-owned. The factors compound rather than cancel. The energy shock raises UK inflation, which prevents the Bank from cutting, which supports a carry premium worth only 7.7 basis points in this pair while simultaneously transferring national income abroad and worsening the fiscal arithmetic through inflation-linked spending — and every leg of that chain ends at 2026-10-28, where the OBR's March headroom of 9.9 billion pounds has almost certainly been consumed by a 39 basis point year-on-year rise in the 10-year gilt at roughly 2.5 billion pounds of debt service per 0.25 percentage point. That Budget lands on the same day as an FOMC decision, which is the one piece of structure in this analysis visible only bilaterally: both legs reprice in a single session and the plausible joint outcome pushes the pair the same way twice. What is priced is a modest fiscal discount on the base leg and a solved-problem view of dollar funding; what is not priced is the terms-of-trade income transfer as a separate additive negative, nor the reserve-scarcity configuration — reserves at 2,916 billion dollars with the reverse repo facility emptied to 702 million — that reproduced the December 2025 squeeze and would push the dollar to the stress side of the smile with London's dollar borrowers as the transmission point. The path of least resistance is lower in two dated steps, the September policy cluster and the 28 October Budget-plus-FOMC session, with the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report and the 2026-12-09 FOMC SEP as the resolutions. Conviction is held at 3 rather than 4 despite the score sitting near the boundary because two of the largest legs are hostage to identifiable events we assess at meaningful probability: a durable Strait of Hormuz reopening at roughly 20 percent would remove the terms-of-trade drag while leaving Bank Rate at 3.75 percent, and a Bank of England hike on 5 November at roughly 25 percent would restore the differential outright.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically GBP/USD ranks as the second most attractive short in the sterling complex, behind GBP/NOK — the purest fundamental mirror of this shock, since Norway's 15.59 percent of GDP surplus is funded by the very prices taxing a 2.8 percent deficit, and a short earns 50 basis points rather than paying — but ahead of GBP/CHF, GBP/SEK and GBP/JPY, all of which are extended and costly to hold. Among dollar longs it falls to roughly fourth over six months, because the dollar itself drops from first to fourth of eleven on the quote dossier's own reckoning, passed by SGD, NOK and SEK on external-balance strength the dollar cannot match. The pair's strategic distinction is that it pairs the G10's most dated idiosyncratic downside event, a 28 October Budget with an OBR forecast, against a quote currency whose own deterioration has no scheduled resolution inside the window.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three weightings drive the divergence. First, consensus treats 28 October as the sterling event and has not marked down the mechanical differential compression available between 16 and 17 September, so we expect the move to start earlier than the quarterly medians imply. Third, consensus prices US fiscal deterioration as a long-end term-premium problem; we weight the transmission asymmetry, in which rising long yields currently buy dollars and sell sterling, so the objectively weaker sovereign is being rewarded — a pair fact neither dossier and no bank note we can find articulates. cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Aligned in direction and conviction, and the thesis deepens modestly with horizon, but the COMPOSITION changes materially and that is the useful finding. The tactical score is 71 percent attributable to two factors, Policy and Rates and Inflation and Growth, both of which resolve on the same two dates and are partly offset by a benign risk regime and a positioning wash. The strategic score has six negative contributors and no positive ones, because weight moves into External Balance and Fiscal exactly where the base currency's structural problems sit and where the transmission asymmetry favours the quote currency, while the two tactical offsets decay: risk appetite loses its informational value once the dominant risks become domestic to each leg, and the sterling short base is being consumed at roughly 10,100 contracts a week and will be largely gone by 28 October. The pair's own option skew corroborates the shape, deepening from minus 0.343 percent at 38.6 days to minus 0.728 at 185.7 days.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The interval between the 17 September MPC and the 28 October Budget-plus-FOMC session carries no scheduled driver — the tactical window resolves the policy differential sign change and the strategic window resolves the fiscal/terms-of-trade thesis.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the two horizons as one thesis expressed in two dated windows rather than as a continuous position, because the interval between them carries no scheduled driver. The tactical window is the 16-17 September cluster, where the differential sign change resolves inside 24 hours and where the ATM surface at 5.654 percent for 38.6 days charges no event premium for two policy decisions. The strategic window is the 28 October Budget-plus-FOMC session and the 5 November Monetary Policy Report, spanned by the 94.7-day tenor at 6.240 percent, only 0.59 volatility points above the front. Because the roll premium is 7.7 basis points, holding through the interval costs almost nothing, which is a genuine advantage over the sterling-complex alternatives — but the negative skew means the directional view is already partly consensus in the option market, so the discipline is sizing rather than direction. In practical terms: run the tactical short at full risk budget into 17 September and take partial profit into the 1.3350-1.3400 area, then re-establish on the retest of 1.3450-1.3550 for the 28 October window rather than holding a single position across both.

catalysts.event: US August non-farm payrolls, unemployment rate and average hourly earnings (consensus +58,000 after −23,000)
catalysts.rationale: The largest two-sided risk before the FOMC and the clearest asymmetry in the tactical window. A second consecutive contraction would make a hike twelve days later very hard to defend, stranding a dollar long of 18,682 contracts and lifting the pair sharply toward the 1.3600-1.3700 area; a firm print removes the labour-market objection, hardens the 16 September hike and compresses sterling's 12.5bp differential toward its sign change.

The cleanest commodity route to the pair rising. Lower crude is mildly pair-positive on the UK import bill and, more importantly, disinflationary for the US, which softens the hike odds carrying Factor 1; higher crude pushes both legs the same way down, since the UK is a net energy importer and the US a net exporter with a reinforced hawkish Fed. Brent has already fallen 12.0% on the month to 88.24 dollars, so the marginal surprise is a supply cut.

catalysts.event: US August CPI, University of Michigan preliminary, monthly federal budget balance
catalysts.rationale: The last inflation print before the FOMC, against a July base of 3.4% headline and 2.5% core. The configuration cuts against the intuitive reading for this pair: core CPI sits 80bp below core PCE at 3.3%, and it is PCE the Fed targets and PCE the Chair quoted at Jackson Hole, so a soft core CPI is less pair-supportive than it appears.

catalysts.event: UK labour market report: unemployment, claimant count, average weekly earnings
catalysts.rationale: The release that most directly determines whether the Bank of England's hawkish tail survives, and therefore whether the pair has any path back to a widening differential. With private-sector regular pay already at 2.8% against a target-consistent estimate near 3.25% and payrolled employees down 210,000 on the year, a further loosening removes the second-round-effects case two days before the MPC votes.

catalysts.event: UK August CPI, core and services CPI; FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The densest single day in the pair's calendar and the point at which the differential can flip. The FOMC is priced at 57-66% for a 25bp hike against a June median dot of 3.8% implying one outright, which would take the bilateral policy differential from +12.5bp to −12.5bp. Simultaneously UK CPI carries genuine upside energy risk that is pair-ambiguous, since it raises hike odds and cuts real income at once.

catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision and minutes, plus the annual vote on the next twelve-month gilt-reduction pace
catalysts.rationale: The rate outcome is close to fully discounted at roughly +7bp, so the information is in the vote split and the QT decision, and the meeting falls the day after the Fed, so the Bank responds into whatever the FOMC has just done rather than setting the tone. A split softening from 6-3 to 7-2 removes the hawkish tail supporting sterling's premium.

catalysts.event: September quarter-end US dollar funding date
catalysts.rationale: The first quarter-end since reserve balances resumed falling, at 2,916 billion dollars heading toward the roughly 3 trillion minimum, with the reverse repo facility drained to 702 million so there is no buffer to absorb balance-sheet compression. Tighter dollar funding moves the quote currency to the stress side of the smile, and the bilateral transmission runs through London's dollar-borrowing institutions.

catalysts.event: UK Autumn Budget with OBR economic and fiscal forecast, AND the FOMC decision — both on the same date
catalysts.rationale: The most consequential dated session of the strategic window and the only one where both legs reprice simultaneously. A Chancellor three months into the job must satisfy fiscal rules whose March headroom of £9.9bn has almost certainly been consumed, with the market already charging 184bp over Bunds; the FOMC meets the same day without projections, so the quote leg's silence is judged in the same session.

The dominant scheduled quote-leg event and genuinely two-sided for the pair. A result constraining fiscal expansion is dollar-positive through the deficit channel and negative through growth; a result enabling it is the reverse; and how either outcome changes political pressure on a Fed that has just hiked over presidential objection is not knowable in advance.

catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision with Monetary Policy Report (projection round)
catalysts.rationale: The largest scheduled upside risk to the pair in the strategic window and the reason strategic conviction is held at 3 rather than 4. First full forecast round after the Budget, the three standing hawks vote again with 2027 pay-settlement evidence beginning to arrive, and the base dossier assesses the probability of a hike at roughly 25% — which would restore the differential outright.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The release at which the 2027 median dot — currently 3.6%, implying a cut back from a September hike — is confirmed or removed. Confirmation means the quote leg's rate support is terminal and fading, which is pair-supportive for the remainder of the horizon; removal converts the September move into a cycle and deepens the bearish case.

The meeting at which the Committee expects to have learned about 2027 pay settlements, the input the July minutes name as decisive for its symmetric reaction function. If private-sector regular pay is still near 2.8% and unemployment above 5.0%, the dovish resolution arrives here and the base leg's hawkish tail is removed for the horizon.

The direct analogue of December 2025, when SOFR-to-IORB spreads reached their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage spiked to a record 74.6 billion dollars on 31 December before collapsing to zero in January. Every precondition is in place and several are worse, and the bilateral channel matters: UK institutions are structurally large dollar borrowers through London's banking role, so a dollar squeeze transmits into the base leg specifically.

invalidators.mechanism: Would restore a positive differential over the Fed's expected November level of about 3.9%, reversing the entire compression mechanism on which a 0.24-weight Factor 1 depends, and would validate three standing hawks the market has written off

invalidators.mechanism: The highest-confidence strategic leg (Fiscal, 62%, weight 0.10) rests on the proposition that the gilt market's sovereign risk premium is a currency premium sterling has not yet paid — a decisive narrowing would show the bond market withdrawing that judgement, removing the mechanism by which the strategic case is expressed in the pair

invalidators.condition: GBP/USD holds a 1.3480-1.3600 range for three consecutive weeks with 20-day realised volatility below 3.0%
invalidators.mechanism: The bearish case requires the September cluster to convert fundamentals into price, and a compression through the cluster into the Budget window would mean the market has judged the differential flip immaterial — with a 7.7bp roll premium there is no carry accruing to compensate a holder for waiting, so a range is a losing outcome rather than a neutral one

assumptions: Price payload quoted verbatim: dataPoints 130; dateRange 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03; spot 1.35243; spotDate 2026-09-03; pipSize 0.0001; computationRange 2007-10-09 to 2026-09-03 (4916 weekday bars); weekendBarsDropped 0. Only 2 resistance / 9 support zones met the 2-touch threshold — supplemented with round numbers and the shortfall noted. Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes and realised volatility is annualised on 252; averages and zones are computed over the whole computationRange, not just the visible 130 bars.

Spot date gap disclosed, not smoothed: spotDate is 2026-09-03, two trading sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date. Every level, target, stop, pip figure, percentage move and distance-to-average is computed against 1.35243; no fresher web quote has been substituted, and the dossiers' alternative spot references (1.35355, 1.3547, 1.35490) are noted but not used in any calculation.

Direction verdict carried, not re-derived: this is pass two of two. The ten factor stances, confidences, evidence_type labels, weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, G10 rankings and cross-horizon consistency text are carried verbatim from a first pass that scored them without the price payload, deliberately. Where price structure disagrees with the verdict — higher lows, positive 1/3/6-month returns, 65th-percentile closing position — that disagreement is stated in prose and left unresolved rather than reconciled by adjusting a number.

Funding premium conflict resolved in favour of the gated store: the gated store reports +7.7bp annualised roll premium (CME calendar spread, 13.6-48.6 days, observed 2026-08-31); the sterling dossier reports 0.0bp observed 26 August and derives a −12.5bp basis. This report uses 7.7bp throughout and derives an implied basis near −5bp, flagged as a derivation with a tenor mismatch; the discrepancy is recorded rather than silently reconciled since it is economically immaterial against 6.240% implied volatility.

Sovereign yield vintages: both legs' 10-year yields in the rates block are monthly observations dated 2026-06-01, roughly 94 days stale, breaching both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows. The +32.6bp differential is quoted only as a like-for-like vintage comparison and never described as a live spread; no analytical weight rests on it. Live readings used in Factor 8 are inherited from the dossiers with their dates attached.

Implied volatility and skew taken verbatim from the gated store, observed 2026-08-31: ATM 5.654/6.240/6.645%; 25-delta risk reversals −0.343/−0.557/−0.728%; butterflies 0.122/0.178/0.214. The three-month figure is measured at 94.7 days, not 90, because CME lists quarterly. The one-year IV percentile (~35) is a labelled estimate inherited from the sterling dossier, not a quote, and no skew-dependent or percentile-dependent conclusion rests on it.

Zone distances: the payload's distancePips and distancePct are measured to zone midpoints. Because the nearest resistance band begins only 23 pips above spot while its midpoint is 52 pips away, both midpoint and near-boundary distances are given for every tactically relevant zone. Zones are ranked by touch count rather than proximity per the framework.

Positioning: sterling's headline −44,500 is legacy non-commercial from the 28 August release (data to 25 August); the leveraged-fund/asset-manager split is from an 11 August tranche, stale by three weeks, and drawn from a different CFTC taxonomy, so the two are not directly comparable. Dollar-index figures are web-sourced because the pipeline COT cache carries no DXY contract. Both percentile readings (~30 sterling, ~80 dollar) are dossier estimates, not published statistics.

Valuation methodology: the 'fair value' of roughly 1.3103-1.3115 is not a PPP estimate. No free PPP source was obtainable for either leg, so the figure is a BIS real-effective-exchange-rate relative — the spot rate at which sterling's June 2026 REER of 111.41 would equalise with the dollar's 107.84. It is a relative-valuation proxy, labelled as such throughout, and the BIS REER period (June 2026) is marginally outside the strategic freshness window.

Bilateral trade: IMF DOTS 2024 goods flows used exactly as supplied and not re-estimated from the web: UK exports to US $73.7bn, UK imports from US $72.7bn, UK net +$1.0bn, against US-reported exports of $79.9bn and imports of $68.1bn. The mirror asymmetry between the two reporting sides is a normal DOTS artefact and is itself used analytically.

Weight adjustments: four adjustments carried from the first pass — Factor 1 tactical +0.03, Factor 3 −0.03 tactical and −0.02 strategic, Factor 5 strategic −0.01, Factor 8 strategic +0.03. Each is within the ±0.05 limit and both weight sets sum to exactly 1.00.

Net stance derivation: both stances were labelled mechanically from the weighted score against the framework threshold (−0.3929 and −0.4316, both beyond −0.10, therefore Bearish). The strategic score sits close to the conviction-4 boundary at −0.45 and is held at conviction 3 by judgement, with the reasoning stated; the stance label itself was not adjusted.

Web research scope: four searches were run, confined to what neither dossier nor the price payload contains — pair-specific bank forecasts and consensus, visually identified chart patterns and named resistance ceilings, pair-specific option-skew commentary, and bilateral gilt/Treasury flow context around the Budget. No spot price, performance figure, moving average, realised volatility level or support/resistance level was taken from the web. Bank consensus is aggregator-reported rather than first-party and flagged wherever used; one retrieved technical source quoted a 50-day moving average of 1.3635 that contradicts the gated store's 1.34488 and was not used.
